citations.review_text: Extremely fun, not too serious especially on lower difficulties, and fun with friends. I like looping the runs and seeing how low my FPS will get as I become a bullet hell demon-crab.

I feel like this game has a lot of good potential, it has a good premise and is all around a good rouge like game. Almost all of the upgrades are balanced and if you play long enough on a run you can out scale the enemies. With that being said like I said before it has a decent amount of potential a few things I thing could need working on or adding would be voice lines for tony and some more story elements.
Overall: 7/10
definity worth the cost if you like rouge like games though it is rough on the edges the core game is very well made.

(while performance isn't really a problem with runs before looping, after you loop you can really feel the fps tank as you get more and more visual effects.)
it´s fun after the 3rd loop performance starts to suffer xD

already fun plus I see the vision. 
main problem is the lag when you turn the power dynamics upside down haha but it's not a huge issue for me actually makes me feel powerful as a matter of fact

claims.claim: This cohort highlights the soundtrack, movement mechanics like sliding and flips, and colourful graphics as standout features.

citations.review_text:
I'm giving it a positive review, as there are a lot of good things and the base is great. The theme is unique (🦀🦀). The soundtrack is obviously a banger. The graphics are nice and colorful. The moment-to-moment gameplay is awesome with the movement feeling very very good (sliding, flips). The cosmetics system is nice and I like the fact that you can unlock anything in-game

However, for me, the game struggles the most with the replay value, and I think this is crucial for roguelikes. You are stuck with one loadout during the run (weapon, skill, melee). Most weapons feel very similar - they just differ in mag size, fire rate, damage, but functionally they are all basically, well, guns. And this wouldn't be much of an issue if we had, let's say, multiple weapons during a run. Maybe with evolutions or some other merge system. Additionally, the perks you find during a run are a bit boring - they are mostly just "deal #% more damage, but with reduced fire rate" or "deal #% more damage, but bullets zig-zag", or a lot of low-% triggers like "you have 3% chance to fire additional shotgun bullets". Most of those upgrades feel like boring stat increases. Besides that, even though the island and enemies look cool, after 3 hours of gameplay, they are getting repetitive

So after I finish a run, I don't have an itch to start another, because the weapon I'll pick will feel similar to the one I just played with, I already know the environment and the monsters and they will be exactly the same again, and the perks I'll pick during the new run won't really affect my gameplay - I will do more damage, but I won't even notice a difference in how I play

I'll be definitely checking out the game after an update

Crab Champions is one of those games that looks like a joke until you actually play it, and then you realise it’s secretly one of the most polished, addictive, and surprisingly deep roguelite shooters on Steam. From the moment you start moving, the game shows off its strongest feature: incredibly smooth and responsive movement. Dashing feels instantaneous and essential, gunplay is crisp and satisfying, and every weapon has a distinct weight and rhythm that makes combat feel tight and deliberate. Enemy waves are short, intense bursts of chaos that keep the pace high, and the arena layouts, while simple, are cleverly varied enough to force different movement patterns and strategies. The whole experience feels like a blend of DOOM’s aggression, Risk of Rain 2’s build insanity, and a crab protagonist who seems permanently furious.

The weapon selection is small but extremely well‑designed. The assault rifle is reliable and perfect for crit builds, the shotgun melts bosses when paired with the right perks, the dual pistols turn into elemental machine guns, the sniper rewards precision with massive payoff, and the rocket launcher is pure explosive chaos. What makes the arsenal shine is how drastically perks can transform each weapon. A basic shotgun can become a poison‑spreading plague cannon, a crit monster that deletes bosses in seconds, or a knockback powerhouse that sends enemies flying off the map. The synergy potential is enormous, and every run feels different because even familiar weapons behave in new ways depending on your perk rolls.

The perk system is the heart of Crab Champions. Every arena gives you a choice of upgrades, and perks fall into categories like damage, utility, defense, and special effects. The real magic is that perks stack aggressively. You can end up with absurd builds like 300 percent crit chance, chain lightning that jumps across entire waves, homing shots that turn every bullet into a guided missile, or ricochet effects that bounce pro…

Listen to me stop thinking and buy this. I ran across this game on accident and played all night 8 hours straight. The art style/graphics are solid and the performance is fantastic. The music is great and the gameplay... the movement in this game and how smooth everything feels is top tier as good as it gets. Reminds me a little bit of Risk of Rain 2 except I enjoy this game much more its turning into one of my fav traditional roguelikes alltime

This game... is so satisfying to play... the smooth movement, the weapon variety, the elements, the special ability triggers, the maps (could do with more maps and biomes) and the amount of cool runs and broken builds you can make here, it's just PERFECT!
I played this game many years ago when the graphics were different and there wasn't as much stuff (skills/guns), so now I'm rediscovering the game and enjoying everything one by one~

cohorts.summary: Reviewers praise the vast array of weapons, items, and powerups that enable diverse builds, alongside robust difficulty modifiers and top tier music.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the soundtrack as high quality and note that it complements the game's atmosphere.

citations.review_text:
This is one of those rare games I always come back to. Whether I want to completely zone out after a long day or get locked into an intense run, it never disappoints. It somehow manages to be both incredibly relaxing and absolutely chaotic when things ramp up.

The soundtrack is genuinely top tier. The music alone makes every run feel better, and it perfectly matches the game's vibe. Buy it.

This game is craaaaaaazy.

The game loop is very simple and possibly repetitive throughout countless runs:
start with a gun, a melee, and an ability; defeat enemy waves to get a power up; buy some more upgrades right before the boss; defeat the boss for better rewards and move on to the next world; do this a few more times and beat the big baddie; end the run to bank the victory or loop from the start for bigger challenges (and another win).
Simple enough, right?

But you also have the opportunity to evolve your choice of powerups in more complex ways - more DPS? Elemental damage? Criticals? Economy? Lifesteal? Speed demon? A mix of all?
And the equipment you bring with you also matters - the same powerups don't work as well on (let's say) high fire rate low damage guns as they would on high power low fire rate ones.

And speaking again of powerups - they come in HUGE numbers. I think there's something like over a hundred different powerups to collect split between gun, melee, ability, skill and relic powerups. Some of them are a no brainer; others require consideration of what you're actually using and how you play the game best.

And if the game doesn't make you break a sweat yet (or too much), you also have modifiers. Those will, in turn, rank you higher if you can complete a loop (or a minimum of two, for even higher difficulties) - but you'd better bring a first aid kit because the game will SLAP you.

And most importantly - you're a crab.
And the soundtrack is just too good. I don't know if it gives anyone else the happy chemicals, but it does to me.

So yeah. The game is very simple to pick up and understand. The first runs will be probably quite easy and give you all the info you need to get good at it. Then it's time to dive deeper into it, and its full potential becomes more apparent.

At the end of the day, this is a simple roguelike third person shooter where you face waves of critters and/or big bad enemies. And you're a crab. And the …
One of my all time games. GREAT music, and super fun once you get good at it. Also easy to lost track of time after playing.
This game not only brings alot of fun and different strategies, but the movement feels great and the music is awesome. Up there with my favorites like Gunfire reborn, and Risk of Rain 2

Genuinely a great value for the money.  The game is pretty simple to get into but as you try and take on higher difficulties it's surprisingly strategic.  Every weapon in the game is viable with the right loadout, and it's really rewarding to take a weapon that feels kinda doo-doo at first and keep trying until you find the right combo of mods, perks and relics until it gets stupidly powerful.

The game is also really fun to play with friends, and cheap and accessible enough that you can just gift a copy to someone if you need someone to play with, if they like shooters at all they'll almost certainly get hooked.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long term players appreciate the adjustable difficulty settings, responsive gunplay, and solid performance, though some point out hidden damage stats until runs end.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that damage taken is not displayed until a run is completed.

citations.review_text: doesnt tell if you have taken damage until you complete the run

This game was honestly a great game to kill time with, challenging, a bunch of weapons and combos to 100%, fun to play with friends. The updates were always fun to come back to and see new enemies, perks and variations of maps. There was always fun to be had playing this, I hope they keep updating, adding and refining this game. there was honestly very few bugs that I encountered while playing this game which is amazing.

I would say that I wish to see variety in the collection of skins, a lot of the skins looked exactly the same for completely different challenges. Of course new weapons, abilities, throwables, perks and biomes are always welcomed. also PvP used to be in the game but was removed for some reason, I actually liked the PvP mode and would like to see it return in the future but with some type of match making for TDM lobbies etc. Parkour was also fun to do in this game, would like that to return as well, maybe add a risk for failing (lose a perk or something). Emotes would also be a fun addition of course. 

Overall this is a great game, my friends and I loved it. We'd love to see more additions to this title. 
After 100% completing this game over 200 hours + , I'd for sure come back and play regularly if there was more challenges/content for me to complete.

9/10 -Too much water

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features adjustable difficulty modifiers and customizable settings for runs.

citations.review_text: Turn your brain off on lower difficulties to have some fun. Amp up the difficulty a bit if you wanna sweat a bit. No metaprogression blocking you from getting far only RNG and the limits of your skills.

The gameplay itself is quite fun,
every gun has unique synergies with unique perks.

The enemies are ez or a pain, some of them are in between.
you'll learn fast wich ones are the strongest.

The difficulty's are quite balanced and customisable,
some modifiers are just there as an extra challenge, i did not use them tho.

Only one bad part of the game was the time that an update added an extra rank,
and i had to do all the weapons again, but thats just me.

Can recommend this game for ppl of this genre.

A brilliantly designed roguelike. The barrier of entry is almost non-existent and the pace is rapid, making it much faster to get into the run and get going than other games in the genre. Weapon and perk design is simple and straightforward, and it is very easy to parse basic information, while there still being tremendous depth and interaction. Difficulty has good customization, allowing for runs with crazy hero moments, or runs where you just snowball entire islands. Plus, you're a crab with a gun, and that's pretty cool

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game has smooth movement and responsive gunplay with an accessible skill ceiling.

citations.review_text:
The build variety is insane, and almost anything is viable with the right combos. Both the movement and gunplay are smooth and accessible with a nice skill ceiling. The way builds can take off scratch the itch to feel like a god.

The best part is you're a crab, and you definitely feel like a champion

Honestly such an enjoyable game.
As a huge fan of roguelike games this is one that has always stood out for me. The concept of it is silly and entertaining, the movement is so free and feels great once you get used to it.
There are a lot of weapons and abilities which make the game play completely different.
Most runs your build will be completely different which is something I love about a roguelike.

It may feel hard at the start but once you learn the basics it becomes something so fun to play

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as performing well with smooth graphics and fast loading into matches.

citations.review_text: Very engaging roguelike shooter. I love the fact that it's so incredibly fast and optimized. I can click play and be in a game within seconds. Graphics are smooth and satisfying, and the game encourages you to break it, and lets you do so.

Very addicting after a few runs, want to 100% but for the last achievement just too lazy to get it but it isn't too hard. Gameplay very easy to understand and not bad performance, unless you make a run breaker build.
